answer: Each identity locks 70 credits for one shard in an orchard archive, with a ferrous tag bound to its key. At an unpredictable slot, an auditor issues an ivory ticket demanding fragment plus tag, ticket consumed per check. Each fake pays 85, 70 locked plus 15 storage, and the kth fake pays the same 85, so 1,000 fakes tie up 85,000. Tickets arrive together, so one operator cannot answer 1,000 at once; each miss burns 70. Rented disks fail: a copied fragment bears the wrong ferrous tag for another key, so it is rejected and its bond burns. Honest agents pay 15 net for one shard and reclaim 70.
